correctness.rationale: The common cubic P(T) for gradient zeros bounds distinct coordinate values by three. Matching e1,e2 for three distinct roots forces all multiplicities congruent to one modulo three; sum nine leaves (1,1,7) and (1,4,4), whose cubic coefficients yield respectively a seven-coordinate zero block and two opposite four-coordinate values. An exhaustive eight-case two-value derivative table rules out other points; constant points are nonsingular. Direct line restrictions verify all proposed lines. Distinctness, degree, integral normal quartic follow. Standalone code symbolically checks all line restrictions and enumerates P^8(F3), where 522 critical points exactly match the union. No finite-field inference is used in the proof over algebraic closure.

Cafure--Matera--Privitelli Section 3 limits the number of distinct coordinates and bounds dimension; its Section 4 treats separate large-characteristic phenomena.

The new claim implies the known dimension in this instance, not conversely.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The proof adds a necessary/sufficient three-root coefficient comparison specific to (p,d,n)=(3,4,9), plus an exhaustive two-value derivative table; these steps are not consequences of the cited general dimension results alone. The degree/characteristic mismatch rules out subsumption by the most relevant accessible prior claims.

value.rationale: The complete 351-line reduced singular-locus classification of a canonical quartic in P^8 detects 315 noncoordinate components invisible to the general dimension and coordinate-local results, despite no dimension jump. Their explicit geometry, purity and degree are natural projective invariants and a starting point for later analysis of the nonreduced Jacobian scheme; the theorem is more than recomputation of known coordinate components.
